title: Query count of sequential disjoint trees
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\Omega$ be a set of coordinate values, and let $\alpha,\beta$ be sets of leaf labels. Consider finite decision trees that query only coordinates in their specified available sets and branch according to observed values. Let $A,B\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be disjoint, let $T$ be a tree using coordinates in $A$, and for each $a\in\alpha$ let $K(a)$ be a tree using coordinates in $B$. For any input $x$, the number of queries in the tree that first runs $T$ and then runs $K$ on the resulting label is the number of queries in $T$ plus the number in $K(T(x))$, each evaluated on $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ and $B$ are disjoint finite sets of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
$T$ is a finite decision tree over $\Omega$ with leaf labels in $\alpha$ and available coordinates $A$
$K$ assigns to each label in $\alpha$ a finite decision tree over $\Omega$ with leaf labels in $\beta$ and available coordinates $B$
$x$ assigns a value in $\Omega$ to each coordinate
